stances.claim: Gesmundo is off to an auspicious start -- he has 5 years and 7 months as runway, the Court has already adopted a zero-backlog plan needing only resolute implementation (July 31, 2007 Resolution), and his fellow nominees plus the rest of the Court have accepted him 'gallantly... without any rancor or reservation,' with Bernabe herself administering his oath.
Gesmundo should this early craft a vision/mission statement and program of action -- and of all institutional priorities, speedy justice (starting with the SC backlog) is the most urgent task.

As an 'OSG thoroughbred,' Gesmundo carries an inclination to uphold government positions in controversial decisions based on the prima facie dictum that official duty had been regularly performed -- a tendency CJ identifies without condemning.

Hernando, the youngest in the Court and only the 4th most senior at 54, will have several chances to be CJ in the future -- and would have been the first 'homegrown' San Beda CJ from the President's alma mater had he been chosen now.
stances.confidence: asserted with personal disclosure ('I would have faded')

stances.claim: Bernabe's track record validates her 'unpredictable on politically-sensitive cases' self-description -- pro-Libingan-Marcos and pro-Mindanao-martial-law on one side; anti-Sereno-ouster, anti-De-Lima-detention, and against the Bersamin 'main plunderer' doctrine on the other -- demonstrating she gives no president undue favor.

Bernabe takes comfort in joining the Honor Roll of venerable seniors who did not become CJ -- J.B.L. Reyes, Herrera, Regalado, Feliciano, Padilla, Carpio -- many of whom 'are revered in history more than some chiefs.'

notable_anecdotes: The Jan 6, 2006 'prophecy' -- CJ Panganiban, then sitting CJ, inducting the unknown-to-him Gesmundo as a Sandiganbayan justice and inviting him to sign his oath in the CJ's chair: 'Please sit down on my chair. One day you will occupy it.' Now 15 years later Gesmundo has taken oath as CJ and thanked Panganiban for the foreshadowing in a phone call the Friday before this column.

Hernando-CJ-counterfactual -- Hernando would have been the first 'homegrown' San Beda CJ from the President's alma mater, and CJ's quietly self-deprecating aside 'I would have faded as the first and only imported chief of the Red Lions' -- playing his own honorary-Bedan status against the prospect of a Bedan-by-formation.

Bernabe's four-president appointment trajectory -- FVR (MeTC 1996), Erap (RTC 2000), GMA (CA 2004), PNoy (SC 2011) -- yet 'she has not given any of them any undue favor,' the quietest possible tribute to non-partisan judicial integrity.

Bernabe's stance set -- pro-Libingan-Marcos AND pro-Mindanao-martial-law AND against-Sereno-ouster AND against-De-Lima-arrest AND disagreement-with-Bersamin-on-main-plunderer -- catalogued as the 'unpredictable conscience' record validating her own JBC self-description.
Bernabe-administering-Gesmundo's-oath -- the symbolic moment of graceful succession from runner-up to chosen, presented as the closing image of an 'auspicious' transition.

The Honor Roll catalog of non-CJ seniors -- J.B.L. Reyes, Ameurfina Herrera, Florenz Regalado, Florentino Feliciano, Teodoro Padilla, Antonio Carpio -- six names of jurists 'revered in history more than some chiefs,' deployed as the formal consolation register.

one_paragraph_summary: Without ubiquitous headlines and TV cameras, CJ Alexander G. Gesmundo quietly took his oath of office on April 5, 2021 and began his 5-year-7-month term as primus inter pares of the SC and leader of the judiciary. Panganiban recalls 'prophesying' Gesmundo's ascent on Jan 6, 2006 -- as then-CJ inducting Gesmundo (whom he didn't yet know) as a Sandiganbayan justice and inviting him to sign his oath in the CJ's chair: 'Please sit down on my chair. One day you will occupy it.' He urges Gesmundo to this early craft a vision/mission statement; of all tasks, speedy justice (starting with the SC backlog) is the most urgent -- and the Court has already adopted a plan in its July 31, 2007 Resolution implementing the recommendations of the Committee on Zero Backlog I (which CJ Panganiban created Jan 26, 2006), needing only resolute implementation. Gesmundo is the third Ateneo Law alumnus (after Claudio Teehankee and Renato Corona) to ascend to the top post, an 'OSG thoroughbred' with SBN, Comelec, and PCGG secondments. Runner-up Ramon Paul L. Hernando, at 54 the youngest and 4th most senior, would have been the first 'homegrown' San Beda CJ (the President's alma mater) and 'I would have faded as the first and only imported chief of the Red Lions.' Senior-most incumbent Estela M. Perlas-Bernabe, 69 on May 14, was named by four presidents to the ascending steps of the judicial ladder (FVR MeTC 1996; Erap RTC 2000; GMA CA 2004; PNoy SC 2011) yet has given none of them any undue favor -- validating her JBC-interview self-description of being 'unpredictable... only when it comes to politically-sensitive cases.' Her catalog shows it: pro-Libingan-Marcos and pro-Mindanao-martial-law on one side; against the Sereno ouster, against the De Lima arrest, and disagreeing with Bersamin's 'main plunderer' doctrine in the GMA plunder ruling on the other. She can take comfort in joining the Honor Roll of revered seniors who did not become CJ -- J.B.L. Reyes, Ameurfina Herrera, Florenz Regalado, Florentino Feliciano, Teodoro Padilla, Antonio Carpio -- 'revered in history more than some chiefs.' CJ closes that Gesmundo is off to an auspicious start, with Hernando and Bernabe (and all his colleagues) gallantly accepting him without rancor and with Bernabe herself administering his oath -- but beyond this felicity, the people expect an independent Court and a judiciary invigorated by speed, integrity, wisdom, and independence.
